blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Image, dress and professional credibility are more tightly connected in British senior life than many international colleagues realise. The rule is not that the most expensive clothes win; it is that visibly appropriate clothes — matched to the room, the occasion and the institution — quietly remove a barrier that the wrong clothes would otherwise place between you and being taken seriously.

At the top, the details matter. Fit. The condition of shoes. The quality of a pen. A senior British colleague will not comment on any of these, but they will register them, and in the moments when credibility is being weighed — a difficult first meeting, an unexpected introduction, a quiet conversation in a corridor — these small signals can make a difference that is very hard to measure and very hard to deny.

The senior lesson is not vanity. It is discipline. Dress in a way that lets your words, your judgement and your experience be the only things people are weighing. Anything that distracts from those three, however small, is a tax on your credibility that you are voluntarily paying.

items.q: According to the text, what do visibly appropriate clothes achieve?
options: They signal that you outspend your peers
They quietly remove a barrier to being taken seriously
They replace the need for good judgement
They guarantee that your arguments will win
items.why: "visibly appropriate clothes… quietly remove a barrier… between you and being taken seriously."

items.q: How does a senior British colleague respond to details like fit or the condition of shoes?
options: They ask you to change them
items.why: "A senior British colleague will not comment on any of these, but they will register them."

items.q: The author frames the 'senior lesson' primarily as a matter of…
items.why: "The senior lesson is not vanity. It is discipline."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The person in the most expensive outfit earns the most credibility
The wrong clothes can quietly cost you before you speak
Image should let your judgement do the talking
Small visual signals matter most in high-stakes moments
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre negando que "the most expensive clothes win" — o argumento é contra equiparar preço a credibilidade.

items.q: Calling a distraction 'a tax on your credibility that you are voluntarily paying' suggests that…
options: distraction is unavoidable at senior level
credibility is a fixed cost you cannot influence
taxes on executives should be lowered
such losses are avoidable and self-imposed
items.why: Inferência: "voluntarily paying" implica que a perda é evitável — você mesmo escolhe pagá-la ao deixar algo distrair.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte preparando o executivo para o primeiro cargo na City de Londres. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before your first week in the City, let me be candid about something no one there will ever say to your face. Nobody is going to compliment your suit, and nobody is going to criticise it either. But they will notice — the fit across the shoulders, whether your shoes are looked after, the watch, the bag. None of it will be mentioned, and all of it will be filed away.

I know that sounds unfair, and in a sense it is. You come from a market where results speak first. Here, in those early weeks, the room is quietly deciding whether to take you seriously, and you want nothing on your person doing the arguing before you open your mouth.

So my advice is simple. Dress a shade above the room, never below it. Choose understated quality over anything with a visible logo — the more conservative the meeting, the more restrained you should be. And treat this as risk management, not vanity. The more you get the image right, the less you will ever have to think about it, and the more your judgement becomes the only thing anyone is weighing.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte say people in the City will do about the executive's suit?
options: Advise him on where to buy one
Notice it silently without mentioning it
items.why: "Nobody is going to compliment your suit… nor criticise it… But they will notice… and all of it will be filed away."

items.q: How does Charlotte contrast the executive's home market with the City?
options: Both markets judge purely on results
At home results speak first, unlike the early weeks in the City
At home image matters more than results
items.why: "You come from a market where results speak first. Here, in those early weeks, the room is quietly deciding whether to take you seriously."

items.q: What is Charlotte's rule about how to dress relative to the room?
options: Dress well below the room to seem modest
Wear the most visible brands available
Dress a shade above the room, never below it
items.why: "Dress a shade above the room, never below it."

items.q: When Charlotte says you want 'nothing on your person doing the arguing before you open your mouth', she means…
options: your appearance should not create impressions that undercut you before you speak
you should let colleagues argue on your behalf
your clothes should never send any signal at all
you should stay silent in early meetings
items.why: Inferência: ela quer que a imagem não fale por você de forma negativa — que nada te prejulgue antes das suas palavras.

items.q: What is the overall attitude Charlotte wants the executive to adopt?
options: Spend as much as possible on clothes
Treat image as strategic risk management
Treat image as vanity to be avoided
Ignore image and rely only on results
items.why: Inferência: "treat this as risk management, not vanity" — ela reenquadra a imagem como gestão de risco, não vaidade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "His attire was visibly appropriate for the boardroom." This means it was…
items.why: Visibly appropriate = visivelmente adequado à ocasião e ao ambiente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The wrong outfit can place a quiet ___ between you and being taken seriously."
items.why: Barrier = barreira; a roupa errada ergue um obstáculo à credibilidade.

items.q: "In those first minutes, the room is quietly weighing your credibility." To weigh here means to…
items.why: To weigh = pesar, no sentido de avaliar/ponderar a credibilidade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Getting the image right is a matter of ___, not vanity — a habit you hold to consistently."
items.why: Discipline = disciplina; a lição enquadra a imagem como rigor consistente, não vaidade.

items.q: "A logo loud enough to distract from your argument works against you." To distract means to…
items.why: To distract = distrair, desviar a atenção do que realmente importa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs de negócios ligados a imagem e credibilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "You never get a second chance to make a first impression." This idiom warns that…
options: the initial impression you create tends to stick
first impressions can always be corrected later
you should delay meeting new people
items.why: Make a first impression = a impressão inicial pesa e é difícil de refazer depois.

items.q: "Understated quality lets him fit in with the City's senior partners." To fit in means to…
items.why: Fit in = integrar-se, pertencer ao grupo sem destoar.

items.q: "A visible logo can send the wrong signal in a conservative boardroom." This means it can…
items.why: Send the wrong signal = passar a mensagem errada, sinalizar algo indesejado.

items.q: "Once your image is right, you can let it slide and focus on the substance." Here 'let it slide' means to…
items.why: Let it slide = deixar de lado, parar de se preocupar com algo que já está resolvido.

items.q: "Getting the small details right helps him hold his own among seasoned partners." To hold your own means to…
options: defer to the most senior person
perform as well as others in a demanding setting
items.why: Hold your own = manter-se à altura, sustentar sua posição entre pares experientes.
